turns.en: But it's this type of interactions and delight that will create a unique experience. And people — even though they can perhaps not point out why they love using this app and why it feels great — it participates unconsciously, I think, in how you perceive the quality of a product you use every day. It's all the little things. For example, on Ammo, on Bump, when you would browse through your friends, the traditional way — or perhaps the first mechanical way you would design it — is just panels or carousels. Perhaps it's a view panel that folds up and then you have cells just like a contact list, you know, the standard way of doing so. And this is how Find My works. This is how Live 360 works. We decided to just go and use existing paradigms and existing communities that are more tactile and more physical to use — like old phones and old business cards. 50 years ago or so, they had this huge Rolodex thing on the desk, which plays as cards, business cards you would quickly be able to go through, or these old phones with wheels. We kind of came up with this idea of having an iPod-like way of browsing your friends as a wheel. You just go through a wheel, and it's fun because when you browse your friends at the bottom of the screen under your thumb, you would see all these faces getting animated when they enter the center of the screen. So they were not animated, and then when they reach the center of the screen you would see your friends being animated and doing crazy things, recording things. It creates really nice anticipation. It creates smiles every time you use such an app. If you're smiling when you use this app even after 45 days, you know you created something really special with users. This is how we would think about it as a whole: the whole experience is one thing, but all the tiny things inside is another one. But it takes time. Definitely today, people say you can build things in two days, go crazy, and ship it. But I think if you spend just two more days — instead of two, spend four days — the quality will be on top, the bar will be raised, and you will have greater chances to create a very delightful product. Or perhaps it will be just 2% or 3% better than the competitor. I think it's fine. It's fine. That because you went through this extra mile of creating great experiences, or because you really wanted this gradient to work, but someone told you, 'Hey, who cares about your gradient? Just ship it.' I think this worked 10 years ago, but it doesn't today.
turns.zh: 但正是这种交互和愉悦感，才能创造出独一无二的体验。而且人们——即使他们可能说不清楚为什么喜欢用这个应用、为什么感觉这么好——我认为这会在潜意识里影响你对一个每天使用的产品质量的感知。全都是这些小事。比如在 Ammo 上、在 Bump 上，当你浏览朋友列表时，传统的方式——或者你设计时最先想到的机械方式——就是面板或轮播。也许是那种折叠起来的面板，然后下面是一格格的联系人列表，就是标准的做法。Find My 是这样做的，Live 360 也是这样做的。我们决定直接用更直观、更有物理感的现有范式和现有社群，就像老式电话和老式名片。大约 50 年前，桌上会有个巨大的 Rolodex 名片盒，你可以快速翻动名片，或者那种带拨号轮的老电话。于是我们想出了类似 iPod 的方式，用转轮来浏览朋友。你转动转轮，会很有趣，因为当你在屏幕底部、拇指下方浏览朋友时，能看到他们的头像在进入屏幕中心时动起来。他们本来静止不动，但一到屏幕中心，你就会看到朋友们做出各种夸张动作、录影什么的。这会带来很棒的期待感，每次用这样的应用都会让人会心一笑。如果用户在用了 45 天后仍然会笑着打开这个应用，你就知道你在用户那里创造出了真正特别的东西。这就是我们的整体思考：整体体验是一件事，里面所有微小的细节又是另一件事，但打磨需要时间。如今确实有人说，你可以两天搞定一个东西，疯狂一把直接发布。但我觉得，如果多花两天——不是两天，而是四天——质量就能达到顶尖，标准会被抬高，你也更有可能做出让人愉悦的产品。也许只是比竞争对手好 2% 或 3%。我觉得这没问题。完全没问题。因为你多走了一步去创造好的体验，或者因为你真的很想让某个渐变效果成立，但有人跟你说：‘别管什么渐变效果了，直接发布吧。’我认为这在 10 年前管用，但现在不行了。

turns.en: And who knows — maybe the models do get incredible to the point where some of the quality bars that you're talking about are able to be hit by the masses. But what you were able to do with Ammo, that is design differentiation, right? Like, that's different. Not necessarily through executing the aggregate of small details. It's differentiation through very creative ideas that are design-driven and truly exist out in left field compared to the sandbox that everybody else is playing in. I'm curious if you have any thoughts reflecting on your journey with Ammo around how did you get there? Like, what does it look like or take to cultivate this atmosphere where those types of ideas can grow and thrive?
turns.zh: 而且谁知道呢——也许模型确实会变得非常厉害，以至于你说到的那些质量标准，大众也能达到。但你在 Ammo 上做到的，那是设计上的差异化，对吧？那是不一样的。不一定靠堆砌所有小细节的执行，而是通过非常有创意的、由设计驱动的想法来实现差异化，而且相对于所有人都在玩的沙盒，这些想法真的是天马行空。我很好奇，回顾你在 Ammo 的经历，你是怎么做到的？比如，要培养一种能让这些想法生长和蓬勃发展的氛围，是什么样的？需要付出什么？

turns.en: It's a really interesting question, and I think it goes both ways. I think sometimes you create something so special and so unique — as a use case — you create new patterns sometimes that are very effective, that people will think about you for this. If you remember Loren Brichter from 15 years ago, who created pull-to-refresh and all these kinds of patterns. And we kind of came up with something similar with the patterns, actually — like the edge zoom on Zenly and Bump, when you have to pull your thumb along the screen. It's kind of hidden, but once you get used to it, you cannot use another map the old way. Every time I open Apple Maps or any new map on my phone for something, I keep going, 'Oh, there is a sidebar on the side, just like a web view basically.' It's crazy. It's so simple, but it's this type of experiences that really stick. And we always think about how we would use it. Do we borrow existing patterns, or do we create new ones? Just like a game — there are infinite games out there, but the UIs, the way you use them, the way you interact with the map, the way you interact with characters, items, guns, or whatever, is always different. There are existing patterns, but there are infinite UIs and UX. And this is how we think about how we design Zenly, how we design Bump, ID, and Tilt, and so on. And sometimes it can go wrong. Sometimes you can ship something like — there are many things that Ammo or Zenly that people just do not get. They would download it and they would be like, 'What's happening? I don't understand what's happening.' So I think it's great to create new experiences and new designs and delightful stuff, but sometimes you're getting lost into it. You're going too far, and people are lost, and you're losing the point, and your users won't understand what's happening. So you have sometimes to go back, step back a little bit, and adjust. And sometimes you will brute-force your way into it, saying, 'Yeah, this is how we do things. This is our DNA. We just ship it and let's roll with it.' And no — if users won't use it, won't do it, or won't pay for it, then you know you're doing something wrong. So it's always kind of — it might feel crazy to use Ammo products, for example, but it's always a game of balance. I think ultimately it's always how you balance things out, and always arbitrage between, 'Is this delightful enough? But wait, did we lose usability? Do we just, you know, have a consensus to go back a little bit?' We also think about word of mouth a lot. Does it have an obvious way to passively attract new users? Because this person will screenshot it, screen-record it, or show it at school, you know, outside, and say, 'Wow, this is amazing. What did you do? Can I try? What's the app? What's the name?' And we never underestimated this, for sure.
turns.zh: 这个问题很有意思，我觉得它是双向的。有时候你会创造出非常特别、非常独特的东西——作为一种使用方式——你会创造出一些非常有效的新模式，人们会因此而记住你。如果你记得 15 年前的 Loren Brichter，他创造了下拉刷新这类模式。其实我们也想出过类似的模式——比如 Zenly 和 Bump 上的边缘缩放，你需要用拇指在屏幕上滑动。它有点隐蔽，但一旦你习惯了，你就没法再用旧的方式去用别的地图。每次我打开 Apple 地图或手机上任何新地图时，我都会想：‘哦，边上应该有个侧边栏，就像网页视图一样。’这很疯狂。它很简单，但就是这种体验会真正烙印在你心里。我们总是会想，我们会怎么用？我们是借用现有模式，还是创造新的？就像游戏——世上有无数款游戏，但 UI、操作方式、你与地图互动的方式、你与角色、道具、枪械等互动的方式，总是各不相同。既有模式是存在的，但 UI 和 UX 有无限可能。这就是我们设计 Zenly、设计 Bump、ID 和 Tilt 时的思路，等等。有时候会出错。有时候你会做出一些东西——Ammo 或 Zenly 里有很多东西人们就是看不懂。他们下载后会说：‘这是怎么回事？我不明白发生了什么。’所以我觉得创造新体验、新设计、让人愉悦的东西是很好的，但有时你会迷失其中。你走得太远，人们会迷路，你会失去重点，用户根本不明白发生了什么。所以你有时需要退一步调整。有时你会强行推进，说：‘没错，我们就是这么做的。这就是我们的 DNA。直接发布，就这么办。’但如果用户不用、不操作、也不付费，那你就知道做错了。所以这始终是一种——用 Ammo 的产品可能会让人觉得疯狂，但永远是一场平衡的游戏。我觉得归根结底就是在权衡，总是在‘这够不够让人愉悦？等等，我们是不是牺牲了易用性？我们是不是应该达成共识，往回退一点？’之间做取舍。我们也很看重口碑。它有没有一种显然的方式能被动吸引新用户？因为这个人会截图、录屏、在学校或者外面给人看，然后说：‘哇，这太棒了。你怎么做的？我能试试吗？这是什么应用？叫什么名字？’我们从来没有低估过这一点。

turns.en: I've been designing products every day for the last 15 years, but in the last 6 months everything has changed. With AI in the mix, I'm cranking out ideas faster than ever. But none of that matters if I can't get the feedback that I need to get the team aligned. And right now, getting async feedback still kind of sucks. So, I'm building the product I've always wanted, and it's called Inflight. I use it every day to share ideas and get feedback from the team, and it's totally changing the way that I work. So, I'm excited to show you. Right now, I'm only giving access to Dive Club listeners. So, head to dive.club/inflight to claim your spot.
turns.zh: 过去 15 年我每天都在设计产品，但最近 6 个月一切都变了。有了 AI 加入，我的想法产出比以往任何时候都快。但如果得不到需要的反馈、不能让团队对齐，这些就都不重要。而目前，异步反馈的体验还是很糟糕。所以，我在打造我一直想要的产品，名叫 Inflight。我每天都用它和团队分享想法、获得反馈，它完全改变了我工作的方式。所以我很兴奋能给你看。现在，我只对 Dive Club 听众开放。请前往 dive.club/inflight 抢占你的名额。

turns.en: I want to toss a hypothetical your way. Let's say that a series A company brings you on.
turns.zh: 我想给你一个假设性问题。假设一家 A 轮公司请你加入。

turns.en: I want everything. And I want this person to be able to code as well. And yeah, I can definitely see that more and more. And I think it's part of our job too, and I know it's your job too, when you're screening new candidates and new talents, to say, 'Hey, this is what you're very strong at, and I have the perfect match for you—the perfect company—you need to talk to them.'
turns.zh: 我想要一切。我也希望这个人能写代码。嗯，是的，我越来越看到这一点。而且我觉得这也是我们工作的一部分，我知道这也是你的工作——当你在筛选新候选人、新人才时，要说：“嘿，这是你非常擅长的地方，我为你找到了完美匹配——完美的公司——你一定要去和他们聊聊。”

turns.en: All right, we covered a lot of ground. I have a random question before I let you go. I'm curious—as somebody who has good taste in consumer products and who's pushing the envelope in interesting ways—is there an app or some kind of product that you've come across in the last year or two where you thought, 'Oh, that is interesting. That did something for me.' Maybe that even tapped into something that feels familiar to the DNA you kind of grew up with in the Zenly and Ammo era.
turns.zh: 好的，我们聊了不少。在放你走之前，我有一个随机问题。我很好奇——作为一个在消费品方面很有品味、并且以有趣的方式不断突破边界的人——在过去的一两年里，你有没有遇到过什么应用或产品，让你觉得“哦，这太有意思了，它真的打动了我”？也许它甚至触动了你在 Zenly 和 Ammo 时代耳濡目染的那种 DNA。

turns.en: Retro app is really great in terms of polish and craft. It's not crazy, but there are all these tiny touches that make it feel like a great app—like the ability to send cool postcards. Almost all the design team from Ammo uses this app on a daily basis, and I'm dragging a little bit behind. I love Duolingo for what they do. The craft—the bar is really high. The design team there is really, really good, and everything is so tightly connected: the brand design, the motion design, the haptics—everything is so, so good. So for me, it's the type of product that is perfect in terms of experience and visual design, in terms of how I feel when I use it. And I have many more that I can't talk about right now, but they're coming up.
turns.zh: Retro 应用在精致度和工艺上真的很棒。它并不花哨，但有许多微小的细节让它感觉像一款出色的应用——比如可以发送炫酷的明信片。Ammo 的设计团队几乎每天都在用这款应用，而我稍微有些跟不上。我喜欢 Duolingo 所做的一切。那种工艺——水准真的很高。那里的设计团队非常出色，一切环环相扣：品牌设计、动效设计、触感反馈——都很棒。所以对我来说，它就是那种在体验、视觉设计以及我使用时的感受上都堪称完美的产品。我还有很多其他的，现在还不能说，但很快就会面世。

turns.en: I love it. Well, I've definitely had fun with this conversation, Julien. I appreciate you coming and sharing the story. It's so interesting, and I'm a big fan of everything you've had a hand in making over the years. So, I'm excited to see what's next, and I appreciate your time today.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢。嗯，这次对话我确实很开心，Julien。感谢你来做客并分享你的故事。这非常有意思，而且我一直都很喜欢你这些年来参与打造的每一个作品。所以，我很期待接下来会发生什么，也感谢你今天的时间。

turns.en: Thank you, Reed. Thank you so much for having me.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，Reed。非常感谢你邀请我。

turns.en: Before I let you go, I want to take just one minute to run you through my favorite products, because I'm constantly asked what's in my stack. Framer is how I build websites. Genway is how I do research. Granola is how I take notes during crit. Jitter is how I animate my designs. Lovable is how I build my ideas in code. Mobin is how I find design inspiration. Paper is how I design like a creative. And Raycast is my shortcut every step of the way. Now, I've hand-selected these companies so that I can do these episodes full-time. So by far the number one way to support the show is to check them out. You can find the full list at dive.com/partners.
turns.zh: 在你离开之前，我想花一分钟带你看看我最常用的产品，因为经常有人问我用了哪些工具。我用 Framer 来建网站，用 Genway 来做研究，用 Granola 在评审时记笔记，用 Jitter 做设计动效，用 Lovable 用代码实现想法，用 Mobin 找设计灵感，用 Paper 像创意人一样做设计，而 Raycast 是我每一步都会用到的快捷工具。这些公司都是我精挑细选的，正是为了让我能全职做这些节目。所以，支持这档节目的头号方式就是去看看它们。你可以在 dive.com/partners 找到完整列表。

consensus.en: Great design is about the little things: thoughtful animations, haptic feedback, and reactions that create a unique experience.
consensus.zh: 好的设计在于那些“小细节”：精心设计的动画、触觉反馈以及交互反应，它们共同创造出独特的体验。

consensus.en: Spending extra time refining details and raising the quality bar can make a product 2–3% better than competitors, which still matters today.
consensus.zh: 多花时间打磨细节、提高品质标准，哪怕只比对手好2%–3%，在今天依然很重要。

consensus.en: Ammo built its entire visual universe around a distinctive motif: animated real-person avatars and a messy 'fridge magnet' collage style.
consensus.zh: Ammo围绕独特母题构建了整个视觉世界：真人动态头像和凌乱的“冰箱磁贴”拼贴风格。

consensus.en: Cross-team collaboration—especially involving backend engineers—generated many of the best ideas at Zenly and Ammo.
consensus.zh: 跨团队协作——尤其是后端工程师的参与——在Zenly和Ammo催生了许多最好的创意。

consensus.en: Side projects are the strongest signal when hiring; they reveal curiosity and entrepreneurial mindset more than pedigree.
consensus.zh: 招聘时，业余项目是最强的信号；它们比出身更能展现好奇心和创业者心态。

contrarian.en: You don't have to make everything purely functional; designing for delight itself can be a strategic product decision.
contrarian.zh: 你不必把一切都做得纯功能导向；为愉悦感而设计本身就是战略性的产品决策。

contrarian.en: When starting a product from scratch, data is useless because it doesn't exist—gut feeling should lead the way.
contrarian.zh: 从零起步做产品时，数据并不存在也没有用，这时候要靠直觉引领方向。

contrarian.en: Backend engineers, not just designers, often came up with the best product ideas—the opposite of conventional hierarchy.
contrarian.zh: 最棒的产品创意往往来自后端工程师而不是设计师——这与传统层级观念相反。

contrarian.en: At top startups, big-company experience can actually hurt you; many hiring managers explicitly reject candidates from companies like Meta or Apple.
contrarian.zh: 在顶尖初创公司，大厂经历反而可能成为劣势；许多招聘负责人明确拒绝来自Meta或Apple的候选人。

contrarian.en: Successful startups now deliberately stay tiny—seven people for years—rather than chasing headcount as a success metric.
contrarian.zh: 成功的初创公司如今刻意保持极小规模——多年保持七人，而不是把人数规模当作成功指标。

contrarian.en: A polished, luxury design direction for Ammo failed because it felt cold and unfunny; warmth and personality mattered more than refinement.
contrarian.zh: Ammo早期精致的奢华设计方向失败了，因为显得冷冰冰、不好玩；温暖和个性比精细打磨更重要。
